summary: Fixes limitations of the Label Distribution Protocol (LDP) wildcard Forward Equivalence Class (FEC) by defining a Typed Wildcard FEC element and its procedures. It also adds an LDP capability for backward compatibility. It is a Proposed Standard.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC adds a more specific wildcard to the Label Distribution Protocol. A router can name the kind of forwarding class it means and use the wildcard when requesting labels.

subtitle: Lets LDP messages target all forwarding classes of a chosen type, including in label requests.

tldr.problem: LDP's original wildcard refers to all forwarding classes and cannot be used in a Label Request.
tldr.mechanism: A Typed Wildcard FEC element names a FEC type to match, and an Initialization capability tells a peer that the feature is supported.
tldr.outcome: Routers can request, withdraw or release mappings for a specified FEC type. RFC 7358 later updates this document.

today: RFC 5918 is a Proposed Standard and is updated by RFC 7358.

sections.title: Limits of the Original Wildcard
sections.content:
The Label Distribution Protocol (LDP) uses Forwarding Equivalence Class (FEC) elements to identify traffic that receives a label. The original wildcard FEC refers broadly to all FECs, with an optional limit to those bound to a label.

That wildcard does not identify a FEC type, and RFC 5036 limits it to Label Withdraw and Label Release messages. This RFC adds a typed wildcard and permits its use in Label Request messages.
sections.plainLanguage: The original wildcard covered every kind of forwarding class and could not be used to ask for labels. This RFC adds a wildcard that names a specific kind.

sections.title: Fields in a Typed Wildcard
sections.content:
A Typed Wildcard FEC element contains its own element type, the FEC element type being matched and the length of optional type-specific information. Its own type is 0x05. The length is zero when no extra information follows.

Without extra information, the element matches all FECs of the named type. A future FEC type specification must define whether typed wildcarding applies and how its optional information is encoded.
sections.plainLanguage: The element identifies itself as a typed wildcard, names the FEC kind, and gives the length of any extra detail. With no extra detail, it matches all FECs of that kind.

sections.title: Using the Wildcard in LDP Messages
sections.content:
The typed wildcard must be the only FEC element in its FEC TLV. If other FEC elements appear beside it, the receiver ignores them and processes the wildcard. A supporting implementation must accept it in Label Request, Label Withdraw and Label Release messages.

A Label Request asks for mappings for all FECs of the named type. For Withdraw or Release, an optional Label TLV narrows the match to FECs bound to that label; without it, all FECs of the named type match. An unknown or unsupported type causes an Unknown FEC notification.
sections.plainLanguage: A request can ask for mappings for every FEC of one type. A withdraw or release can do the same, optionally limited to one label.

sections.title: Announcing Support to a Peer
sections.content:
An LDP speaker that supports the typed wildcard must include a Typed Wildcard FEC Capability Parameter in its Initialization messages. The capability gives a peer a way to learn about support before it sends a message using the new element.

The capability TLV type is 0x050B and its length is 0x0001. The U and F bits are set to 1 and 0, and the S bit is set to 1 to advertise support.
sections.plainLanguage: Routers announce support during session initialization. A peer can then know that typed wildcard messages are understood.

sections.title: Prefix Wildcards and Security
sections.content:
This RFC defines typed wildcarding for the Prefix FEC type. The FEC type value is 0x02, and its extra information contains a two-octet address-family value. The RFC excludes the removed Host FEC type and the already-untyped Wildcard FEC type.

The RFC adds no security considerations beyond base LDP. It notes that a typed wildcard can limit one message's effect to one FEC type, unlike the original wildcard, which can affect all types.
sections.plainLanguage: The specified prefix wildcard can be limited by address family. Restricting a request to one type can limit its effect compared with a wildcard for every type.
